discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulating and superconducting states

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics / nanoscale and 2D materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group achieved this precise twist and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, turning a simple rotation into a knob for strongly correlated physics. The results have been reproduced by many laboratories around the world and extended to orbital magnetism, Chern insulators, and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moire materials. 'Twistronics' created a new field. It showed that stacking and rotating atomically thin crystals can produce designer quantum matter, bridging nanoscale fabrication and fundamental many-body physics. Few recent discoveries have so changed what we believe can be built at small scales.
